title: Elderly neighbor welfare rotation
summary: A respectful check-in rotation for older neighbors during heat, cold, outage, smoke, water cut, or isolation without exposing private medical details.
content: Core sequence: 1) List only the address, preferred contact method, check time, and practical support agreed by the person. 2) Use two short check windows per day and mark no-answer separately from refused help. 3) Ask about water, temperature, phone charge, medicines available today, and whether a trusted contact should be called. 4) Escalate to family, building manager, local authority, or 112 when there is danger, repeated no-answer, confusion, or unsafe indoor heat or cold.
